title: How do I get access to OAuth institutions?
snippet:
### If you're on a Trial plan
[Trial plan](https://plaid.com/docs/account/billing/#trial-plans) customers have access to all [OAuth institutions](https://plaid.com/docs/link/oauth/) without completing the full [Production](https://plaid.com/docs/quickstart/glossary/#production) registration requirements. Plaid collects the necessary information during Trial plan signup, so you do not need to separately provide application display information, company information, the MSA addendum, or the [Plaid security questionnaire](https://dashboard.plaid.com/overview/questionnaire-start). You can start connecting to OAuth institutions right away.

title: How are Sandbox, Production, Trial plan, and Limited Production different?
snippet:
Trial plan and Limited Production are two ways to access Production for free, on a limited basis, before applying for full paid access.

| | Sandbox | Production (full) | Trial plan | Limited Production |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cost** | Free | Paid | Free | Free |
| **Data** | Mock | Real | Real | Real, with usage caps |
| **Item limit** | Unlimited | Unlimited | 10 Production Items | Capped |
| **Approval** | None | Required (a few business days; company + use-case info) | Auto-approved for most developers | Required |
| **Availability** | All developers | All developers | US/CA developers, signups on or after April 15, 2026 | Existing Limited Production customers only (no new US/CA signups after April 15, 2026) |
| **Best for** | Building and testing without touching live data | Deploying your application | Trying Plaid with real data before committing to a paid plan | Legacy free-tier access for existing customers |

For developers in the US and Canada who sign up on or after April 15, 2026, Plaid offers a [Trial plan](https://plaid.com/docs/account/billing/#trial-plans) — a free way to use Plaid with real production data before applying for full Production access. Trial plans are auto-approved for most developers and support up to 10 Production Items.

title: plaid.com/docs/account/billing
snippet:
#### Partnerships pricing
If you are using a Plaid partner, you will be charged for Plaid API usage performed by the partner using your processor token in the same way as if the calls had been made by you. The partner's API usage will not be included in your Plaid Dashboard [usage report](https://dashboard.plaid.com/activity/usage) . If you have questions about the partner's API activity, contact the Plaid partner.

title: What is the Plaid Trial plan?
snippet:
The Plaid Trial plan provides free access to Plaid's production APIs. You can connect real financial accounts, call production endpoints, and build projects — no business registration, security questionnaire, or sales process required.
## Who can sign up
The Trial plan is available to developers who:
- Are located in the United States or Canada
- Do not already have an existing Plaid Production or Limited Production account
US and Canadian institutions are available on Trial plans, all other institutions are not currently available on this plan type. To get started, go to [dashboard.plaid.com/signup](https://dashboard.plaid.com/signup).
## Agreements
Applying for a Trial plan requires accepting Plaid's standard Master Services Agreement (MSA).
In the Agreements step of the application you'll check "I agree to the latest Plaid Master Services Agreement," along with attestations about keeping your accounts, data, and code secure. The application can't be submitted without these.
## What's included
The Trial plan includes access to the following products:
- [Auth](https://plaid.com/docs/auth/) — retrieve account and routing numbers
- [Transactions](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/) (including Recurring Transactions and Transactions Refresh)
- [Balance](https://plaid.com/docs/balance/) — retrieve real-time account balances
- [Identity](https://plaid.com/docs/identity/) (including Identity Match) — retrieve account owner information
- [Assets](https://plaid.com/docs/assets/) — generate asset reports
- [Liabilities](https://plaid.com/docs/liabilities/) — retrieve loan and credit card data
- [Investments](https://plaid.com/docs/investments/) (including Investments Refresh)
- [Statements](https://plaid.com/docs/statements/) — retrieve bank statements

The Trial plan includes immediate access to almost all [OAuth](https://plaid.com/docs/link/oauth/) institutions, including Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo, Capital One, Citi, Navy Federal, PNC, U.S. Bank, American Express, and Merrill.
You don't need to complete the OAuth registration requirements in the Dashboard until you upgrade to a paid plan.

title: plaid.com/core-exchange/docs/implementation-checklist
snippet:
*   Get access to the Plaid Data Partner Dashboard. Your Plaid contact will provide a one-time use link to either sign up for a data partner Dashboard account or create a new team if you already have Plaid Dashboard access.

_(This section only applies to existing Plaid partners)_
If your institution is already supported in [Plaid Link](https://plaid.com/core-exchange/docs/user-experience/index.html.md) or you are a [platform provider](https://plaid.com/core-exchange/docs/onboarding-guide/index.html.md#integration-models-single-institution-vs-platform) with numerous institutions, Plaid will partner with you to develop a pilot and migration plan.
A typical migration involves:
1.  **Pilot cohort:** Enable new connections in production for a small cohort, monitor health, and resolve issues.
2.  **Remaining cohorts:** Expand to remaining cohorts in production, with continued monitoring. The number of cohorts is partner-dependent.
3.  **Existing user migration:** After integration health is validated, Plaid begins a process to migrate all existing Items over to the OAuth + API connection. This phase typically runs over approximately 90 days.

title: plaid.com/docs/account/resellers
snippet:
The Reseller Dashboard and API are functionality that Plaid has developed to support our authorized Reseller Partners. If you don't have a formal partnership established with Plaid, [contact us](https://plaid.com/contact/) to learn about signing up or to receive the appropriate contractual agreements to unlock this functionality.
#### Overview
This guide explains how an authorized Plaid Reseller Partner can create and manage their End Customer teams. Each one of your End Customers is required to have a unique set of Plaid API keys, which enables reporting their billable usage, filing and managing support issues, customizing their Plaid Link experience, and registering their applications with our financial institution partners.
#### Configuring your Reseller Partner team
When you join the Plaid Reseller Partner program, you will work with your partner account manager to set up a Reseller Partner team for your company.
Get started by [signing up](https://dashboard.plaid.com/signup) for a Dashboard account, which will automatically create a team for you. Next, talk to your partner account manager to configure your team as a Reseller Partner team.
If you already have a Plaid Dashboard account, or are using Plaid for a separate use case or business line, we require that you create a separate Reseller Partner team. You can use the same Dashboard user account (email address) to access both teams.

If you expect to onboard a large number of End Customers, or if you'd like to minimize the amount of manual work required by your operations staff, we strongly recommend that you integrate with our [reseller API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/partner/index.html.md) , which allows you to programmatically incorporate End Customer creation and management into your onboarding flows.

Being a member of a Reseller Partner team automatically grants you permission to create and manage End Customers. However, you must first switch to your Reseller Partner team in the Dashboard to exercise these permissions.
